content:
Arriving at Zayed International Airport (AUH) is simple if you know the order of events: immigration first, then baggage and customs, then one arrivals hall where everyone exits. Your passport needs six months of validity, cash over AED 60,000 must be declared, and if you have pre-booked a chauffeur your driver is already standing in that hall with a name board. This guide walks a first-time visitor through the whole thing, from the jet bridge to the car door.

What does a first-time visitor need to know about AUH at a glance?

FactDetailSource
AirportZayed International Airport (AUH), Abu Dhabi. Terminal A is the main terminal and the Etihad hubExperience Abu Dhabi
Passport validityAt least six months beyond your date of entry, machine-readable and in good conditionZayed International Airport
Cash declarationAny amount over AED 60,000 (or equivalent) must be declared; gifts capped at AED 3,000Zayed International Airport
Where private drivers meet youInside the arrivals hall, at the designated area for pre-arranged transfersZayed International Airport
Where friends collect you by carShort Stay Car Park directly opposite the terminal; vehicles must not be left unattendedZayed International Airport
Bus to DubaiAirport Express to Ibn Battuta Bus Station, hourly around the clock, about 90 minutes on the timetableZayed International Airport
Wi-FiFree and unlimited across the terminal on the "Zayed International Airport Free Wifi" networkZayed International Airport

What should you have ready before the plane doors open?

Get these out of your bag while you are still taxiing, because immigration at AUH moves quickly and you do not want to be the person holding up the queue.

  • Passport with at least six months of validity left, as required by the airport's entry rules
  • Your visa or entry permit, printed or on your phone, unless you qualify for visa on arrival or GCC visa-free entry
  • Your hotel name and address, in case an immigration officer asks where you are staying
  • Your chauffeur booking confirmation, with the pickup name you gave at booking
  • A phone that works on Wi-Fi, so you can message your driver on WhatsApp if you need to
  • A note of anything you need to declare at customs: cash over AED 60,000, gifts over AED 3,000, medication
  • A jumper. Abu Dhabi is hot outside but the terminal is air-conditioned hard

How does immigration work at Zayed International Airport?

You go straight from the gate to the immigration counters, and there is nothing to fill in on the plane. The airport's arrivals guide tells you to proceed directly to immigration on disembarking, with Smart Gates available to UAE residents and eligible nationals for faster processing.

Who needs what depends on your passport. GCC citizens enter visa-free with a passport or national ID, citizens of eligible countries get a visa on arrival at the counter, and everyone else must hold a visa or entry permit before they fly, according to the airport's visa, passports and customs page. Check the UAE Government Portal for your own nationality before you book, because the airport itself says the rules change.

First-time visitors on a visa on arrival should expect a short wait at the counter while the officer scans your passport and takes a photo. It is routine. Keep your phone away and have the passport open at the photo page.

Where do you collect your bags and clear customs at AUH?

Baggage reclaim is directly after immigration, and your carousel number is on the information screens by flight number. The terminal guide puts it plainly: check the screens, collect from the designated carousel, and use the Customs declaration lane if you have anything to declare.

If you have nothing to declare, you walk straight through. The cases where you must stop are spelled out on the customs page: cash or financial instruments over AED 60,000, gifts worth more than AED 3,000, and restricted goods such as certain medications or large quantities of tobacco. If you are not sure about an item, declare it, because the penalty for not declaring is worse than a five-minute conversation.

Porters are available if you have more bags than hands. Once you pass customs you are in the public arrivals hall, and that is where the airport ends and your journey into the city begins.

Where does your chauffeur meet you in AUH arrivals?

Inside the hall, holding a board with your name on it. The airport's terminal guide confirms that pre-arranged private transfer drivers meet passengers at the designated area in arrivals, so you never have to go outside and look for a car.

With an Abu Dhabi airport transfer from Emirates Limo, the chauffeur is tracking your flight number and is already in position when you clear customs. He greets you, takes your luggage, and walks you to the car parked nearby. You do not need to phone anyone, find a taxi rank, or work out which car park you are in.

Your flight being early or late does not matter. The pickup time moves automatically with the actual landing time, and Emirates Limo gives you 60 minutes of free waiting at the airport counted from when the wheels touch down. That covers a slow immigration queue and a late bag, with no extra charge.

If you cannot see the board, stay inside the hall and message +971 56 996 4924 on WhatsApp. The airport Wi-Fi is free and unlimited, so you do not need a local SIM to reach us. Do not go outside to the taxi bays or the car park, because that is exactly where drivers and passengers lose each other.

What are the ways to get from AUH into Abu Dhabi?

You have four realistic choices: a pre-booked chauffeur, an official airport taxi, a public bus, or a rental car. The right one depends on how much luggage you have, whether you are travelling with children, and how much you value walking out of arrivals and straight into a car.

Pre-booked chauffeur. The airport's own taxis and limousines page describes independent luxury operators offering fixed-rate, high-end vehicles, and recommends pre-booking so the driver is waiting when you land. That is exactly what a chauffeur pickup at Zayed International is: a private car reserved for your party, a fixed price agreed at booking, and a driver in the hall with a name board.

Official airport taxi. Metered taxis run 24 hours a day from the bays directly outside the arrivals hall, with wheelchair-accessible and larger vehicles available, according to the airport. They are a fair option for a solo traveller with one bag, and you pay the meter at the end.

Airport Express bus. This is the budget route to Dubai rather than into Abu Dhabi. It runs hourly, around the clock, from AUH to Ibn Battuta Bus Station in Dubai, with tickets from a counter in the arrivals hall, and the published timetable shows a 90-minute journey.

Rental car. Car rental desks are in the arrivals hall for anyone who prefers to drive. For a first visit, be honest with yourself about driving an unfamiliar motorway system after a long flight, especially at night.

How long does it take from Zayed International Airport to the city or to Dubai?

Allow around 30 to 40 minutes to central Abu Dhabi and around 90 minutes to Dubai, and add time in the morning and evening rush. The airport sits on the mainland east of Abu Dhabi island, so every route into the city crosses one of the bridges, which is where traffic builds up on a weekday.

The Dubai run is a straight motorway drive up the E11, and the airport's own bus schedule budgets 90 minutes for it. In a chauffeur-driven car with no stops it is about the same, and the price you paid at booking does not change if traffic makes it longer. Abu Dhabi charges a toll through its Darb gates at peak hours; in a chauffeur-driven car there is nothing for you to register or pay at the gate.

If you are landing at AUH but staying in Dubai, book the Abu Dhabi airport to Dubai transfer rather than a city transfer and a second car. The chauffeur meets you in arrivals in the same way and drives you door to door to your Dubai hotel.

What goes wrong on AUH airport pickups, and how do you avoid it?

The same handful of mistakes account for nearly every missed pickup at Zayed International, and all of them are avoidable with a minute of care at booking time.

The wrong flight number. Flight tracking only works if the number on the booking matches the flight you are on. Put in the operating carrier's flight number from your boarding pass, not a codeshare number from a partner airline, and update us on WhatsApp if you are rebooked.

Walking outside. Passengers who cannot spot the board go out to the taxi bays or the Short Stay Car Park, which the airport reserves for private pickups by friends and family. Your chauffeur is inside the hall, so stay put and message us.

Changing the plan late. A different hotel, an extra passenger, a child seat you forgot to mention: all fine, but tell us before the day. Emirates Limo confirms child seats at booking, and a six-passenger GMC Yukon or Mercedes-Benz V-Class cannot appear at the kerb if the booking says a sedan.

Assuming the free waiting is unlimited. It is 60 minutes from actual landing time at the airport, which is generous but not infinite. If you know you have a long immigration queue ahead, for example a visa on arrival for a family of five, message the driver and he will hold.

Cancelling too late. Cancel 24 hours or more before pickup for a full refund. Inside 24 hours, and for no-shows, the booking is charged in full, so if your flight is cancelled by the airline the night before, cancel the transfer straight away.

Which vehicle should you book for your group?

Book by luggage count, not just by heads. A sedan such as the Lexus ES300 takes four passengers and three bags, the BMW 7-Series and Mercedes-Benz S-Class take three passengers and three bags, and a family with suitcases and a pushchair needs the GMC Yukon or Mercedes-Benz V-Class, each of which carries six passengers and six bags.

The full fleet list shows every car with its passenger and luggage capacity, and the booking form only shows you vehicles that fit your group. If you are on the fence, size up: the price is fixed and nobody has ever complained about too much boot space after a long-haul flight.

How do the options compare on cost and convenience?

Every fare from Emirates Limo is fixed at the moment you book, so the comparison below is about what you pay for and what you get, not a price list. Get an instant quote on the service page for your own date, vehicle and destination.

The last row is worth a second look if you land in the morning and want to see the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque or the Corniche before check-in. An hourly chauffeur collects you at AUH, keeps your bags in the boot, and waits at each stop, so your first day is not wasted on a hotel lobby.

What should you do in the first ten minutes after landing at AUH?

Turn your phone on, connect to the free airport Wi-Fi, and check WhatsApp for a message from your chauffeur. Then walk to immigration with your passport open, collect your bags, pass through customs, and look for your name in the arrivals hall.

That is the whole arrival. Ten minutes of admin, a short walk, and someone is carrying your bags to a cool car. Book your private AUH transfer before you fly, and the only decision left when you land is whether to nap on the way to the hotel.

faqs.question: Where do private drivers meet passengers at Zayed International Airport?
faqs.answer: Inside the arrivals hall, at the designated area for pre-arranged transfers, according to the airport's terminal guide. faqs.question: How long is the drive from AUH to Abu Dhabi city centre?
faqs.answer: Around 30 to 40 minutes in normal traffic, longer in the morning and evening rush when the bridges onto Abu Dhabi island slow down. Dubai is around 90 minutes up the E11, which matches the 90 minutes the airport's own Airport Express bus timetable allows.

faqs.answer: Nothing you need to act on. Emirates Limo tracks the flight number on your booking, so the pickup time moves automatically with the actual landing time, and 60 minutes of free waiting at the airport starts from touchdown. There is no extra charge for a late flight.

GCC citizens enter visa-free, citizens of eligible countries get a visa on arrival at the immigration counter, and everyone else needs a visa or entry permit before flying, according to the airport's visa and customs page. faqs.question: Can I cancel an Abu Dhabi airport transfer if my plans change?
